newsitem.title: EGYPT: Shares fall in subdued trade on Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Shares fall in subdued trade on Cairo bourse.

text.p: Shares fell on the Cairo bourse in volume swollen by trade in Egyptians Abroad for Investment and Development on Sunday, brokers said.
The Capital Markets Authority overall index ended down 2.98 points at 361.17 points.
Brokers said volume of about 38 million pounds ($11.19 million) was swollen by 15.9 million pounds worth of trade in shares in Egyptians Abroad.

"Such transactions do not reflect the market," said Mohammad Abdullah, Intercapital managing director. Abdullah said the high trade in Egyptians Abroad investment company appeared to be a transaction organised between the buyers and sellers of the share.
"Most shares were stabilised in an unusually quiet day."

Abdullah added that there was still a "buying opportunity" and anticipated a rejuvenated market in early June when he thought the stock market would be listed on an International Finance Corporation (IFC) index.
Many fund managers trade on the IFC investable index and brokers have said the listing would raise the market profile.
Helwan Portland Cement was the second most active share with shares worth 2.19 million pounds changing hands. The share closed 0.3 pounds down at 74.4.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 515.06 points from 522.06 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms fell to 261.59 from 263.01.
